heroHeadline: CENTCOM Declares Hormuz Mines Cleared and Iran's Oil Exports at Zero; IRGC Navy Fires Back, Claims 'Decisive Control' of the Strait
heroSubtitle: Day 183 (August 29, 2026): The war's six-month mark brought dueling, irreconcilable claims over the Strait of Hormuz rather than new strikes. CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper announced Aug 27-28 that international shipping lanes had been fully cleared of Iranian sea mines, with nearly 1,500 vessels and ~750 million barrels of crude escorted through under the naval blockade since mid-July, ~75 vessels turned back and 3 disabled for non-compliance, and Iran itself exporting zero oil since the blockade resumed. The IRGC Navy rejected this outright on Aug 28-29, declaring 'decisive control' of the strait and accusing US officials of lying about its status to manipulate energy prices; the White House told Al Jazeera the blockade remains fully active and confirmed no talks are underway with Tehran. Separately, SNSC secretary Mohsen Rezaei said Iran is compiling formal conditions for reopening Hormuz — ending the regional war, lifting the US blockade, war-damage compensation, and sanctions removal — while Iran's Foreign Ministry blasted the new 'Operation Economic Outcast' sanctions package as 'economic terrorism' and urged all countries to defy it. Actual shipping traffic remained near-collapsed regardless of the competing claims, at roughly 10 vessels/day versus a 130-140/day pre-war baseline; Brent crude ticked back up to ~$88.58/bbl. No new strikes or casualties were reported on Iranian territory or against Gulf shipping in the two days since Aug 27, consistent with the conflict's now-established pattern of economic and information warfare over kinetic escalation.
